svg.title: How Certificate Transparency works
svg.desc: The CA sends a precertificate to two or more logs run by different operators. Each log returns a signed certificate timestamp (SCT), a promise to publish within 24 hours. The CA embeds the SCTs in the final certificate. The browser refuses certificates without enough valid SCTs. Monitors read the logs and tell domain owners about every certificate for their names.

text.tspan: the log does not judge: it accepts any chain to a trusted root.
it only makes issuance public. Judging is the monitors' job.
and nothing here, yet, proves a log kept its promise: Parts 04 and 05.
